Era già buio e sono passata di fianco al fieno senza pensare che c'era il buco

Mi è mancata la terra sotto i piedi

Mi sono sentita precipitare

Sono atterrata con il sedere
Ho preso un chiodo da trave (che serviva per legare i vitellini quando non c'era più posto nella stalla) nella schiena e per il contraccolpo ho sbattuto la testa nella parete di destra

Basta che non pesi più del terzo

stories.title: 24 novembre 2018 — i Pietrobon "Bóni" (sito di Mariano Berti)
stories.text:
Sito, 19:15: [foto di una coppia anziana seduta] Fiorino era il capo carismatico della famiglia dei Pietrobon soprannominati Bóni, che dirigeva a bacchetta come un direttore d'orchestra. Poteva anche sembrare burbero e autoritario, ma sotto la scorza ruvida nascondeva un cuore indulgente. Sua prioritaria preoccupazione era mantenere unito il nucleo familiare per il bene comune; non era un istruito, ma a questo fine usava tutta la sua…
Family Tree, screenshot 20:01: …tedesco, compositore e direttore d orchestra. Giuseppe e Santa furono genitori di Giacomo (1826), che il 25 maggio 1880 convolò a nozze con Maddalena De Rossi (1830, "Fermi"), ma anche di Giovanna (1828), di Angelo (1830), di Antonia (1837), di Elisabetta (1841) e di Antonio (1848). Dall unione di Giacomo e Maddalena nacque Teresa (1855), quindi Pietro (1860), colui che esportò i Pietrobon a Padernello accasandosi con Giovanna dei "Marconatèi", dando origine alla discendenza dei "Bóni" per distinguerla dal ceppo originale di Paese, tuttora chiamato "Pierobóni". Pietro e Giovanna furono precursori di quattro discendenti, tre maschi e una femmina. I capostipiti Zuane e Anzola (Giovanni e Angela) erano quindi nati nell epoca barocca quando musicisti come Albinoni (1671-1750), Benedetto Marcello (1686-1739), Vivaldi (1678-1741) e Tartini (1692-1770), tanto per rimanere nel Veneto, componevano autentici capolavori destinati all…
Family Tree, screenshot 20:55: …Emilia, Trentino, Liguria, Campania e Basilicata. In Padernello arrivarono all alba del 1882 provenendo da Paese (Treviso-Italia), quando Pietro (1860-1944), lasciando la casa colonica che i "Pieroboni" occupavano quali fittavoli dell Opera Pia S. Maria dei Battuti di Treviso, si sposò con Giovanna Marconato (1861-1953, dei "Marconatèi") dando origine ad una nuova discendenza. In questa giovane frazione di Paese, che era stata comune autonomo dal 1806 al 1866, abitavano tra le Vie Ortigara e Sottana, in un grande edificio con cinque porticati, di fronte al campanile della chiesa, nell area che in seguito vedrà l insediamento della ditta Montini, fabbrica di bilance per pese pubbliche e sbarre per passaggi a livello e carri ponte ferroviari. Sembra anzi che un tempo l edificio fosse stato una delle tante residenze monastiche sparse nel territorio, poi espropriate. Pietrobon sembra derivare proprio da Pietro bon (buono). Non sappiamo quando…

stories.title: 18–19 agosto 2020 — chat con Remo Pietrobon: la battaglia del Piave
stories.text:
08:12 Remo: Hi Massimo,
I'm very interested in the first word war in Italy, in particular the Second Battle of the Piave River fought between 15 and 23 June 1918, because I'm sure it was this attack by the Austro-Hungarian army on the morning of the 15th that my father told me about how they were woken early in the morning by bombing and how my nonno quickly gathered a few belongings in a wagon and left the fighting and went to stay somewhere far away for many months.
He told me that when he returned to his home,obviously after the battle of Vittorio Veneto, that it looked to him that his house had been in a battle area.
I'm wondering if you can find out if your father's house was in the battle area.
I have done quite a bit of research and know that the Italian army crossed Fiume merlo a few times and I thought the battle was very close to Monestier de Treviso, so that's pretty close to your house.
I wonder if you know where to look to find out?
Remo
10:34 Massimo: Remo, the stories you gathered are impressive!!! wonderful!!! I love them! they are a sort of lost fragments of the same puzzle we can have here. This specific part of the family story was lost here. my father and my mother remember that they flew away from the battle. It's amazing now imagining how hard it was for them to stay far from the hose for so long and waiting the end of the conflict... and coming back, after so long... finding such a scenary.
10:47 Massimo: indeed all you know is completely correct: Monastier was one of the most important place of battle during the second attack of the Piave river. this second attack is called "the Solstice Battle". and there's a very popular song they create for this event (it's a military march, but it was proposed to be the Italian national anthem several time in the last decades). Also Ernest Hemingway was there during the was period. He was placed in Monastier di Treviso itself and he was injured during the fights, they brought him in a local house used as a military hospital and there he was also baptized. Part of these events are written in the book "a farewell to arms". Anyway, the local monastery of Monastier was bombed and destroyed during this long battle. A lot of places in Monastier now have signs and descriptions telling about the WW1 fights and events. The beginning of the battle was launched by the Austro-Hungarian army during the night (2.00 a.m. approximately), also this is confirming the stories we listened.
10:50 Massimo: there are lot of rests of war in our fields. I remember that my father always came back from the agriculture works with some rusty medals, some bullet, some rest of coin of this period and things like this. We still used for years a baionette as a conventional knife for all the works in the field... but it was a WW1 weapon we found in our lands!
10:52 Massimo: sometimes there are people in the village that are organizing some expositions about what they found in their fields. here you have an example: [link a lavitadelpopolo.it sulla mostra di Angelo Brisotto a Monastier]
11:05 Massimo: look at this map of the front battle that I found out [mappa]
11:06 Massimo: I overlapped a local map with the name of the villages in order to know exactly the place of Candido's house (Monastier was called Fornaci at that time) [mappa con "Candido's House"]
13:14 Massimo: can you visualize this family tree that I made in the FamilySearch web site? I hope so: [link FamilySearch] and this is the song (a bit too military and patriotic for my personal point of view... but this is history, also). here you have the song: [link YouTube]
23:52 Remo: Thank you very much, I can see from the overlap on the map that the battle certainly was around your house.
My father told me that when he returned to his home, there was shrapnel and bullet damage to the house.
And now looking at the map I can see why.
He said there were rifles, grenades and other equipment scattered around.
Thank you again.
Remo.
By the way I'm very impressed in your ability to write English,
